title: Which Entry Path?
context: Three incidents are reported on the same day. You must identify the vector of each to guide controls.

n1.text: An employee scanned a QR code on a poster and entered their credentials on a spoofed page. Which vector?

choices.why: The QR code is an image that hides the URL: it is an image-based vector.
NFC/Bluetooth are signals; a QR code is visual content.

n2.text: The second incident: a SaaS provider hosting your email was compromised and its access was used against you. Which vector?

choices.why: The trusted third party is the entry path: it is the supply chain.
The network is used afterward, but the origin is the vendor.
No physical impersonation is involved here.

n3.text: Third incident: lateral movement via PowerShell on an already compromised server, with no new file. Which vector and which control?

choices.text: Endpoint-based (living-off-the-land): behavioral telemetry and restriction of native tools
choices.why: Built-in tools are an endpoint-based vector: they are detected by behavior, not file signature.
The vector is already internal to the endpoint.

n4.outcome: You classified the three incidents by entry path and proposed controls suited to each vector.

debrief: The vector family depends on the entry path, not the final tool used.
QR code = image-based; compromised SaaS = supply chain; native tools = endpoint.
QR/RCS and Bluetooth/RF/NFC are framework vectors absent from the provided books.
